origins: When prayers about rent, bills, or work seem to go unanswered, silence can feel like neglect. People who were overlooked as children, whose needs were forgotten by caregivers, often carry the same expectation toward God. The longer the need lasts, the more natural it feels to say, “He has forgotten me.”
teaches: God anticipated this fear. Through Isaiah He asks, “Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you! Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands.” Jesus tells us that not one sparrow is forgotten by God and that we are worth more than many sparrows. He says our heavenly Father knows that we need these things. Paul promises that God will supply all our needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus. Waiting is not forgetting.
self_statements: He answers everyone else’s prayers but mine.
My needs are too small or too ordinary for Him.
I have been waiting too long.
He has moved on from my situation.
No one is looking out for me, not even God.
errors: Feeling forgotten and concluding that I am.
Treating a delay as a refusal.
Noticing the unmet need and missing past provision.
Predicting that God will never come through.
questions: When have I been overlooked by people, and how has that colored how I see God?
What provision, large or small, have I received that I did not earn?
Is waiting the same thing as being forgotten?
What does God say about forgetting His children?
What needs of mine has God already met?
What am I asking Him for, and what can I do while I wait?
truth: God has not forgotten me. He has written my name on the palms of His hands. He knows what I need before I ask. Waiting is hard, but it is not abandonment, and I can keep trusting Him and taking sensible steps.
hw_truths: My name is on His palms.
The Father knows what I need.
He cares for the sparrows, and I am worth more.
log: Each day, write one thing you received that you did not earn or arrange: food, kindness, a door opening.
actions: Write ten times God or His people met a need of yours.
Write each need plainly and tell God about each one.
Tell a trusted friend or church member about one need and let them help.
Read it aloud each morning for a week.
prayer: Lord, I feel forgotten. Thank You that You say You cannot forget me. Show me how You have already provided, supply what I need, and give me patience while I wait. Amen.
hw_questions: When have I felt overlooked by people?
What needs am I bringing to Him?
Is waiting the same as forgetting?
Who could help me with one need?
What can I do while I wait?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God has written my name on the palms of His hands, so He has not forgotten me.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “God has forgotten my needs.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
